object_description: linear block along the square with a polygonal internal circulation and three atriums
geometry_property: storey added in the second stage
design_condition: a linear body runs along the square and forms the end of the park, with the gymnasium partly underground and the second stage realised as an added storey

positive: The spatial organisation cleverly responds to the context, with hall, gymnasium and bicycle area activating the facades
The rigid volume is characterised by an innovative floor plan disposition along a polygonal corridor
Access and rooms widen and narrow so that zones and recreational areas allow spontaneous, individual use
Three atriums group the vertical access, connect floors and uses and provide structured orientation
The innovative and well-researched richness of the interior is convincing architecturally and pedagogically
The clear urban approach and its consequences in the floor plan are evaluated positively
A slightly meandering path of variable width creates an interesting sequence of differently sized spaces
The long corridor becomes an inspiring experience space and the open plan a stimulating learning landscape
The unusual layout offers a high degree of pedagogically valuable rooms and room groups
The compact economical volume and the extension as an added storey are cost-effective and sustainable
negative: The classrooms tend to be too elongated
The basic level lacks a connection to the outdoor space
The slight gradient of the middle floors appears unnecessarily forced and is criticised as uneconomical
The linear body acts as a barrier between the two districts and cuts off access to the park
Too little use is made of the open space of the park and contact between school rooms and park is limited
The outdoor space sits on the roof of the gymnasium, which detracts from its proximity to nature
The roof outdoor space creates a break between the school building and the all-weather playground
Second-stage units have no direct access to outdoor space and must share it with the first stage
The new extension represents an unnecessary impairment of the north facade of the historic building
The gymnasium ceiling beams appear rather narrow for the three-storey building above
The lift shaft planned between the gymnasium ceiling beams can only be implemented to a limited extent
The sloping floor levels unnecessarily complicate the detailing
